beats.text: If you lived somewhere sunnier, you'd be happier. Right?
Researchers asked almost two thousand students in California and the Midwest how satisfied they were with their lives.
But both groups predicted that Californians would be happier.
When you imagine a life, you zoom in on one thing. The weather.
When you actually live it, the weather is a tiny part of your day.
Psychologists call this the focusing illusion.
The researchers put it simply. Nothing that you focus on will make as much difference as you think.
So that one thing filling your head right now? It might be smaller than it looks.

sources: Schkade & Kahneman (1998). Does living in California make people happy? A focusing illusion in judgments of life satisfaction. Psychological Science 9(5). 1,993 students (Michigan, Ohio State, UCLA, UC Irvine). Own life satisfaction equal across regions; both groups predicted Californians more satisfied; difference mediated by climate. Closing line: 'Nothing that you focus on will make as much difference as you think.'
